newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Liberian parties want poll delay, candidate says.
newsitem.headline: Liberian parties want poll delay, candidate says.

text.p: Fifteen of the 16 political parties due to take part in Liberia's May 30 general election want it delayed to August or September to ensure credible results, the only woman presidential candidate said on Wednesday.
Ellen-Johnson Sirleaf told reporters in Lagos that only Charles Taylor's National Patriotic Liberation Front wanted the presidential and legistative elections held as scheduled.

"We have submitted our position paper to Nigerian head of state General Sani Abacha in his position as chairman of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)," Sirleaf said, adding: "All the parties have a consultative meeting with General Abacha on Thursday in Abuja (the Nigerian capital)."

Liberia's former warlords, now presidential candidates, have arrived for the talks in Abuja, which will next week host a meeting of the ECOWAS Committee of Nine on Liberia to finally decide whether or not to postpone the polls.
Sirleaf said the parties wanted the polls held in August or September because May 30 was not feasible logistically.
The May date was part of the peace plan brokered in Abuja last year by ECOWAS and backed by the Nigerian-led African peacekeeping force ECOMOG.

"We believe that without resolving problems associated with the elections the results will not be seen as free, fair and credible by Liberians and the international community," said Sirleaf, who resigned as United Nations Development Programme Africa director to join the presidential race.

"We believe the technical expertise to conduct the elections is not ready. There is need to educate Liberians on the entire voting process. There is also the issue of repatriation of Liberian refugees in time for the elections."
Apart from killing more than 150,000 people, the Liberian civil war, launched in 1989 by Taylor but now ended by ECOMOG, displaced half the country's pre-war population of 2.5 million.
Hundreds of thousands of Liberians are refugees in neighbouring Ivory Coast, Guinea and Sierra Leone. Others are in Ghana and Nigeria.
Liberia was founded by freed American slaves in 1847.
